records.title: A ridge-based detection algorithm with filament overlap identification for 2D mycelium network analysis
records.software_license: MIT-style permission notice documented in repository README; verify exact repository snapshot before use

data_rights.notes: Repository README says the project contains ground-truth skeletons for Cardini_et_al_images and states software license terms. Underlying source image rights must be checked separately. Repository also documents manual visual assessment/correction for selected branch/crossing cases.

records.published_sample_summary: 135 real mycelium images across multiple datasets, species, backgrounds, contrast levels and acquisition systems; reported filament detection F1 0.88–0.94 and crossing F1 0.89.
records.independent_unit: Source specimen/acquisition session; reconcile image-to-specimen mapping before assigning splits.
split_requirements: Keep images from the same specimen and acquisition session in one split.
Reproduce manual correction/adjudication cases separately from fully automated scoring.
Use source dataset/species/device group holdouts for domain-shift evaluation.
known_limitations: Selected branch/crossing evaluation cases require manual visual adjudication/correction according to the repository README.
2D projection cannot resolve arbitrary z-order or true 3D contacts.
Software licensing does not establish rights to every embedded source image.
source_manifest_requirements: Exact Git commit and file digests
Annotation revision and manual adjudication receipt

records.title: Three-dimensional graph reconstruction of filamentous structures from z-stack images
records.software_license: Permissive MIT-style software license text in Zenodo record; verify exact package version and any third-party components

data_rights.notes: Zenodo record identifies some embedded data subcollections as copyrighted by Oscar Sten and the 2D source images as copyrighted by Cardini et al. (2020). Software license is not a blanket grant for all images, annotations or third-party material.

records.published_sample_summary: Public software package record describes fungal z-stacks, 2D fungal images, time-lapse images, overlap annotations, printed-filament prototypes and source scripts. Paper reports overlap F1 0.91–0.92 on six manually annotated real fungal images; separate 3D printed prototypes provide known-geometry tests.
records.independent_unit: Biological specimen/stack or printed-prototype/acquisition run; preserve those groups and their repeated frames.
split_requirements: Keep every z-plane and time frame from a specimen/stack in one split.
Separate printed-prototype geometry from real-fungus evaluation.
Do not describe six manually annotated overlap images as comprehensive 3D ground truth.
known_limitations: Overlap F1 0.91–0.92 is reported on six manually annotated real images.
3D printed known-geometry evaluation is not biological-network ground truth.
Data subcollections have distinct copyright notices; file-level rights review is required.
source_manifest_requirements: Zenodo record/version and exact package file digest

records.title: A travelling-wave strategy for plant–fungal trade
records.software_license: MIT (analysis code, as stated by the paper)

data_rights.notes: Paper states main-analysis and figure source data are on Figshare and analysis code is MIT. Record the data artifact's own license and any third-party restrictions per file before redistribution.

records.published_sample_summary: Study tracked more than 500,000 fungal nodes and linked approximately 100,000 bidirectional cytoplasmic-flow trajectories to growing network coordinates across three AM fungal strains.
records.independent_unit: Independent fungal network/plate and strain/experimental cohort; exact replicate map must be recovered from source files.
split_requirements: Keep all frames and trajectories from one network/plate in one split.
Hold out biological replicate and, separately, fungal strain for transfer tests.
Retain simultaneous antiparallel stream observations as separate directional series.
known_limitations: Plate-based network growth is constrained to 2D and is not full 3D soil-network truth.
Figure/source data are not automatically equivalent to all raw microscopy acquisitions.
No cross-split leakage from tracks, crops or frames from the same network.
source_manifest_requirements: Figshare article version and file digests

records.title: Cytoplasmic flow dynamics in arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are intrinsic and independent of plant hosts

data_rights.notes: Article data availability statement says all data are available upon request. Do not treat supplement videos as a complete raw trajectory dataset or assume data reuse rights; request files, metadata, replicate mapping and license terms from authors.

records.published_sample_summary: Article reports 5,000 cytoplasmic-flow videos and approximately 25,000 trajectories from two Rhizophagus irregularis strains.
records.independent_unit: Biological replicate/network, strain and acquisition series; obtain the mapping from authors before any split.
split_requirements: Keep all videos/trajectories from the same biological network in one split.
Stratify by strain and treatment after obtaining replicate identity.
Record unavailable/failed acquisitions and all measurement censoring.
known_limitations: Raw data are request-only according to the article.
No public raw dataset should be presumed accessible.
Flow trajectories are intrahyphal observations, not isotope delivery measurements.

records.title: Feeding of Agaricus bisporus Mushrooms is Impacted by Mycelium Colonization Time and Network Architecture

data_rights.notes: Article states raw data are available on Figshare and the article is CC BY 4.0. Verify the Figshare artifact's own license, file list and reuse terms independently.

records.published_sample_summary: Stable-isotope source-to-sink analysis in Agaricus bisporus; supplementary table describes 23 fruiting bodies from three independent cultivation boxes in flush one. Individual mushrooms show heterogeneous isotope incorporation.
records.independent_unit: Cultivation box (the paper treats box culture as the biological/experimental unit for treatment analyses); mushrooms are subsamples.
split_requirements: Keep all mushrooms, flushes and repeated assays from one cultivation box in one split.
Use box-level resampling and confidence intervals.
Preserve missing, censored and below-detection tracer outcomes.
known_limitations: Individual fruiting bodies within one box can have heterogeneous uptake.
Graph reachability and spatial proximity are not direct measures of isotope delivery.
The article's license does not by itself establish the raw Figshare artifact license.

records.title: A microfluidic platform reveals the role of liquid movement on the dispersal of Pseudomonas putida via Pythium ultimum hyphal highways

data_rights.notes: Article states data are available on Zenodo and analysis macros are included in supplementary material. Verify the exact Zenodo record's file-level license and version before redistribution.

records.published_sample_summary: Hyphal Highways Device study of Pseudomonas putida dispersal along Pythium ultimum under unsaturated conditions; article reports outlet CFUs in 4 of 8 co-inoculated devices, with non-arrival outcomes retained.
records.independent_unit: Independent device/culture run; verify replicate/device IDs from raw files.
split_requirements: Keep all videos, frames, channels and measurements from one device/culture run in one split.
Preserve devices without outlet CFUs as non-arrival/censored assay outcomes.
Do not treat bacterial dispersal as cytoplasmic or nutrient transport.
known_limitations: The study is a controlled microfluidic assay, not a complete soil-network model.
Only 4 of 8 co-inoculated devices yielded outlet CFUs; exclude-success-only analysis is biased.
Liquid distribution and hyphal biomass influence observed bacterial movement.
source_manifest_requirements: CFU detection limit and non-arrival coding

records.title: Fungal Network Analysis — multi-taxa microscopy images and processing parameters
records.software_license: Fungal Network Analysis software package is separately versioned at Zenodo; packaged v1.00.24 requires MATLAB 2024b or uses Windows standalone. Pin exact archive/build before comparison.

data_rights.notes: Zenodo record 5725751 exposes a blank License field; OpenAIRE indexes CC BY for the record, but validate the actual file-level metadata and source-image rights before reuse or redistribution. Do not infer data rights from the software package.

records.published_sample_summary: 3.2 GB of mycelial images from basidiomycetes, ascomycetes and zygomycetes, with associated species keys and Fungal Network Analysis processing parameter files.
benchmark_tasks: graph topology and ecological trait reproduction
records.independent_unit: Original fungal specimen and acquisition image series; recover specimen/source grouping from names_key.xlsx and source metadata.
split_requirements: Keep images from the same specimen/acquisition series in one split.
Hold out fungal taxa and acquisition conditions separately for domain transfer.
Reproduce FNA parameters and report tuning budget; do not tune on the final holdout.
known_limitations: Zenodo's visible License field is blank, although OpenAIRE indexes CC BY; file-level rights require verification.
This is principally image and parameter data; it is not a calibrated 3D contact ground-truth benchmark.
FNA's connectivity-preserving over-segmentation followed by edge pruning is a strong baseline and must be reproduced rather than approximated.
source_manifest_requirements: FNA software build and parameter files

records.title: Fungal Network Grazer Analysis — four-species time-series images and processed data
records.software_license: FungalGrazers R repository license and FNA binary license are separate; inspect/pin each before execution or reuse.

data_rights.notes: The Zenodo record exposes a blank License field. It contains legacy experimental images from Crowther et al. (2011), parameter files and processed outputs; verify source image rights and reuse permission per artifact before redistribution.

records.published_sample_summary: 10.2 GB across four fungal species (Hypholoma fasciculare, Phanerochaete velutina, Phallus impudicus and Resinicium bicolor) growing from wood-block resources over compressed soil, with and without invertebrate grazers. ZIPs include original time-series images, FNA parameters and processed outputs; FNA version 1.00.24 is identified in the record.
records.independent_unit: Independent soil-box/wood-block experiment and fungal species/replicate. Recover the exact experimental-unit map from source metadata before splitting.
split_requirements: Keep all frames, images, parameter files and processed outputs from one wood-block/soil-box replicate in one split.
Use leave-species-out and leave-treatment-out tests in addition to replicate-held-out tests.
Do not treat individual frames or processed edge measurements as independent replicates.
known_limitations: The Zenodo record's visible License field is blank; source image rights require clarification.
Dataset was produced with FNA v1.00.24; compare using that pinned processing version and report deviations.
Ecological treatment/time-series data are not 3D geometry or direct measurements of cytoplasmic/resource flux.
source_manifest_requirements: FNA v1.00.24 parameters and software archive
Data rights/permission by original image source

records.title: SkelPy — fungal skeletonization software and example images
records.software_license: Repository license must be checked at the exact code commit; do not assume the article's CC BY-NC 4.0 license applies to the code or example images.

data_rights.notes: The paper states that the SkelPy repository contains source code and example images. The full 180-image time series is not stated as publicly available. Check the GitHub repository's code and example-image license separately; article CC BY-NC terms do not automatically apply to repository contents.

records.published_sample_summary: The paper's study imaged three Botrytis cinerea isolates in liquid culture over 72 hours at 20 four-hourly timepoints (180 time-series images). It also reports a throughput run of 3,842 images. Only code and example images are stated as publicly available; the full raw 180-image series should be treated as author-access dependent until confirmed.
records.independent_unit: Independent fungal isolate/culture replicate and well/plate series; all timepoints from a biological series must remain together.
split_requirements: Do not split 20 timepoints from one well/series across train and test.
Use leave-isolate-out and biological-replicate-held-out evaluation.
Separate node-level validation (30 images) from spatial-grid cell validation (30 sampled cells).
Do not compare its grid-cell F1 directly with a crossing-detection F1 from another task.
known_limitations: SkelPy's image acquisition was consistently focused at the bottom of each well and constitutes a 2D planar projection, not complete 3D network truth.

The article reports a 0.0046 normalized-image-width mean nearest-skeleton distance, node precision 80.8% on 30 images, and a separate spatial-cell F1 of 0.905 from 30 sampled cells; these are distinct protocols.
The full 180-image raw series is not identified as a public download; only code and example images are stated to be available.
The article's CC BY-NC 4.0 license does not establish repository-code or example-image licenses.
source_manifest_requirements: Exact Git commits for SkelPy and downstream R analysis
Per-file code/example image digests and licenses
Imaging plane, scale and calibration metadata
Author permission for full raw image series if requested

records.title: The mycelial network organization adapts to facilitate new substrate colonization and fruiting in Agaricus bisporus

data_rights.license_label: Article: CC BY (Utrecht University research portal)
data_rights.notes: The article is listed as CC BY by the Utrecht University research portal. Confirm the raw Figshare record's own license, file-level terms and any third-party image/metadata rights before reuse or redistribution.

records.published_sample_summary: Longitudinal imaging of Agaricus bisporus vegetative colonization and fructification. Optical grayscale intensity is used as a proxy for substrate colonization density; cord abundance is quantified by surface area, with cord widening observed during mushroom development. Directional extension into newly encountered substrate and cord formation in new and pre-existing regions are reported.
benchmark_tasks: cross-validation against independent isotope source-to-sink outcomes
records.independent_unit: Recover the biological replicate, cultivation box, substrate region and imaging-series mapping from the raw data and methods before splitting; do not treat frames or image crops as independent units.
split_requirements: Keep every image/timepoint/region from one biological replicate and cultivation box together unless the published design defines a different independent randomization unit.
Do not split repeated scans, crops or multiple substrate regions from the same cultivation unit across train/test.
Use held-out cultivation replicate and, separately, held-out substrate/demand condition for transfer evaluation.
Keep isotope transfer outcomes from the companion study as a separate outcome family and match replicate identity only where the experimental design supports it.
known_limitations: Grayscale intensity is a colonization proxy, not a direct measurement of fungal biomass.
Cord area and width are structural measurements, not direct conductance or flux observations.
The reported association between demand/development and cord formation does not establish a causal effect.
Raw Figshare artifact rights and replicate mapping must be verified before ingestion.
source_manifest_requirements: Figshare record/version and per-file content digests
Image acquisition timepoint and stage labels
Spatial calibration, scale and coordinate transforms
Analysis code/version and cord segmentation/area/width methods
Missing, censored and unavailable image regions
